source.note: Explanations are read from the activities named as each step's source. Every figure is copied verbatim from the section of EVAL_REPORT.md it cites; backEnd/tests/unit/test_developer_workflow_content.py fails when a figure, heading or path no longer matches.
source.components_note: Each step's `components` are the registry components (basis/prompts names, or what a harness stands for in backEnd/evals/record.py HARNESS_COMPONENTS) whose run records the dialog lists from GET /v1/ops/eval-runs; a review step lists none.

roles.VISION_SURFACES_MODEL: Surfaces, materials and room identity, one call per photo
roles.VISION_FUSION_MODEL: Count fusion: second countables call, fused per class
roles.ROOM_MODEL: Room reconciliation, one call per multi-photo room
roles.ROOM_MATERIALS_MODEL: Material second look (wainscoting, wall finish, tile)

roles.CLASSIFY_MODEL: Residual classifier: components no convention or rule decides

how.title: Register and upload
how.detail: Each appraisal and photo is registered with its sha256, uploaded to a signed URL that lasts 15 minutes, then confirmed. A lost upload is resumed by re-issuing the URL; the same file registered twice at once is handled safely.

how.title: Intake, then start
how.detail: Start is refused until the intake (property use, placed-in-service date, state, basis) and an appraisal are present. The study's first revision and its Temporal workflow are created together.

how.title: A worker takes it
how.detail: A worker polling the basis-studies task queue records the run start, moves the study to extracting and fans out the appraisal and photo activities in parallel. A worker loads its embedding model before it polls, so the first ingest cannot miss its heartbeat.

results.summary: An engineer registers each document, uploads it to a signed URL and confirms it; start is refused without the intake and the appraisal (37.1), and a fresh worker now loads the embedding model before it polls so the first appraisal ingest cannot miss its heartbeat (39). Capacity was load-tested per worker process (32): about 6.6 studies an hour at the defaults, 104.0 with the launch settings.

how.title: Ingest the report PDF
how.detail: ingest_appraisal picks the extraction source (a PDF, a UAD 3.6 ZIP, or a bare MISMO XML's companion PDF), parses its layout, chunks the text per page with whole tables kept, embeds the chunks and publishes the study corpus, so every citation names its source document.

how.title: Read the fields
how.detail: A UAD 3.6 XML is read directly, with highlight regions from the PDF. A PDF gets Azure Document Intelligence's page text and one grounded call on EXTRACTION_GROUNDED_MODEL that reads every field with a verbatim quote, each value checked against its quote; when that call cannot run, the Azure DI pipeline with one TEXT_MODEL call fills the fields still missing.

how.title: Validate and gate
how.detail: Values are checked (types, ranges, presence rules, cross-field consistency) with their sources kept; a missing or conflicting critical field flags the appraisal review, where the engineer's corrections overwrite fields as source manual.

results.summary: Appraisal reading was compared across Azure DI's own key-value pairs and 1004 model, the Azure DI pipeline with a model fallback, grounded one-call readings on five models and two-model votes (33.5). Production reads a PDF with one grounded call on gpt-6.1-sol (EXTRACTION_METHOD=grounded, 33.12), falls back to the Azure DI pipeline with gpt-6-luna when that call cannot run (17.3, 18), and reads a UAD 3.6 XML or ZIP with the MISMO reader (33.7).

how.title: Prepare and count
how.detail: analyze_photo resizes, strips EXIF and re-encodes each photo, then makes two concurrent structured calls: countable objects on VISION_MODEL and surfaces, materials and room identity on VISION_SURFACES_MODEL, merged into one analysis with one components row per kind.

how.title: Fuse counts per class
how.detail: A third concurrent countables call on VISION_FUSION_MODEL supplies the count for the classes where it measured better (the per-class table of section 15.4). The stored analysis records which model gave each count; a failed second call keeps the base counts and flags the photo instead of failing it.

how.title: Outline every object
how.detail: localize_photo sends the photo's countable labels as phrases to SAM 3 in one full-frame prediction; every instance is stored as box and mask, counted when its score clears its class threshold, so an engineer can inspect and select objects. It runs behind the rooms review and never fails the study.

results.summary: Each photo gets narrow calls instead of one call for everything: countables on gpt-6.1-sol at low effort, with a second countables call on claude-opus-5-5 at medium effort fused per class (15.4), and surfaces and room type on gpt-6-luna (28.1). The decomposed step beat the one-pass prompt (11, 12.1), detectors and segmenters did not beat the model counts (21.6, 26.2), and SAM 3 runs after the model only to draw highlight masks (19, 30).

how.detail: Photos whose file names name the same room, plus the engineer's room aliases, share one room; the model's room identity groups a photo only when its name says nothing. Grouping by the model alone merged distinct rooms, and grouping without aliases counted views of one room twice.

how.title: Name, type and floor
how.detail: Each room is named from its file name without the floor, typed from the name's words first and the photos' room answers second, and floored from the file name first. A change is a room.voted event naming the source of each field; a room the engineer corrected is never re-voted. No model call is made.

how.title: Open the rooms review
how.detail: The rooms review opens once every photo is analyzed and voted. Ambiguous photos stay in Unassigned, SAM 3 outlines continue in the background, and a photo whose analysis failed keeps its failure code for the engineer.

results.summary: Photos are grouped into rooms by file name plus the engineer's room aliases, with the model's room identity only as a fallback, because the model's grouping merged distinct rooms and the no-alias grouping counted views of one room twice (23.3, 27.1). Each room is then named from its file name without the floor, typed from the name's words first and the photos' vote second, and floored from the file name first; this makes no model call (48.4).

how.title: Rebuild each room's input
how.detail: reconcile_rooms reads the approved room's photos in file-name order with each photo's component rows (so corrections carried into the revision are what is reconciled) and the prepared images from storage. A room whose photos did not change keeps its inventory.

how.title: Count each component once
how.detail: A one-photo room takes its photo's analysis as its inventory. A multi-photo room gets one room_inventory call on ROOM_MODEL that lists every component once across the room's photos, with the photos it was seen in. An unusable answer falls back to the heuristic merge and flags the room.

how.title: Second look at materials
how.detail: Wainscoting, wall finish and tile get a material second look on ROOM_MATERIALS_MODEL (from Mask2Former surface crops when MATERIALS_SECOND_LOOK=surface_crops). The result is one components row per component with raw.source = room_inventory, which process_assets uses instead of the per-photo rows.

results.summary: One-photo rooms take their photo's analysis as the inventory; each multi-photo room gets one reconcile_rooms call (room_inventory/v3) that counts every object once across the room's photos, then a material second look on wainscoting, wall finish and tile on claude-sonnet-5-5 (16.5). The reconciliation moved from Sonnet 5.5 to gpt-6-luna at the same accuracy for less than half the cost (28.2, 31); one call per room with all its photos counted better but ships off by default until a second property confirms it (26.10, 29).

how.title: Classify
how.detail: Each component is classified by the firm's conventions first (prefetched by context key), then the IRS rules table with the component's room, then the bounded residual classifier on CLASSIFY_MODEL, whose tool calls search the reference corpus and the study's own appraisal. Every model answer keeps its citations, verified against the chunk text; a convention outranks a model answer at every tier.

how.title: Measure and price
how.detail: Quantities come from the appraisal's areas (gross living area shared over rooms by type weight, basement and garage areas, footprint and site for property-level rows), measured once per room and takeoff row. Each row is priced from the RSMeans cost table at the study's year index and location factor, with the full cost trail written on the row.

how.title: Add the structure and reconcile
how.detail: The structure model prices the concealed systems from the RSMeans square-foot model (or the appraisal's cost approach), carves out what the photos evidenced, depreciates the whole and reconciles the total to the purchase price less land. A gap outside the tolerance flags the assets review and withholds the allocation.

results.summary: Each asset is classified by the firm's rulings first, then the IRS rules table, then the residual classifier on claude-sonnet-5-5 at low effort with BM25 search over the reference corpus, kept because no cheaper model matched (17.3, 28.3) and the hybrid search only tied (25.2). Dollars come from the RSMeans cost table with a cited year index and location factor (45, 47), the RSMeans square-foot structure model with the carve-out for the concealed systems (44), and four sourced method corrections that make the depreciated total reconcile to the purchase price less land (49).

how.title: Promote the rulings
how.detail: After the assets approval, promote_conventions turns the engineer's corrections and the cited model answers of the approved revision into the firm's conventions, so the next study's identical component is classified from them at no cost.

how.title: Export the revision
how.detail: export_report writes the approved revision as canonical JSON (extraction, rooms, components, the evidence pack with citations, provenance, timeline) and a CSV of its assets. The same revision exports byte-identical files with the same sha256.

how.title: Record the spend
how.detail: summary.spend rolls up every paid call by stage, activity, component, model and kind (calls, tokens, dollars, latency), and rev-n.calls.jsonl is the transcript of each call with its prompt and raw response. Exporting files does not complete the study: Report & sign does.

results.summary: The results step exports the approved revision (canonical JSON, CSV, evidence pack, spend rollup, draft report and the preparer's schedule); across the live runs the corrected study on the final build is the best result so far, and the printed report reproduces the export to the cent (63). Every paid call is in the study's ledger with its tokens and dollars (40).

how.title: Complete details
how.detail: The firm profile and the study details the report needs are saved. The report is rendered from the export with Typst, chosen because it produced byte-identical PDFs on the Mac and in the Linux worker image.

how.title: Preview and sign
how.detail: An engineer or owner opens the preview; signing re-renders it and compares the sha256, refusing a changed preview or revision (412 BASIS-REPORT-010). The signature row, the report.signed event and the signed PDF are written together under one Idempotency-Key.

how.title: After signing
how.detail: A signed PDF is immutable. A later change to the inputs marks the study changed since signing; Start a new revision reopens the assets review, re-exports and signs the next revision while the earlier signed PDF stays byte-identical.

results.summary: Typst was chosen to render the study report because only it was byte-identical between the Mac and the Linux worker image, and faster (51.2); the engineer signs the preview they opened, re-rendered and compared by sha256 so a stale preview is refused (52), and the whole step, including a new revision after a signature, was verified end to end on an isolated stack (72).
